ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: The first empire to span the subcontinent, with a bureaucracy ahead of its time.
The conqueror of Kalinga who turned to dhamma and carved his conscience onto rocks and pillars.
The classical age: mathematics, poetry and temple art under a light imperial hand.
Three centuries of sultans who made Delhi one of the great capitals of the Islamic world.
The city of victory that ruled the south and awed every traveller who saw it.
From Babur to Aurangzeb: the richest empire on earth in its day.
The Mughal who ruled by inclusion, debating every faith at his court.
Grief in white marble: the empire's wealth and craft in one building.
The confederacy that broke Mughal power and dominated eighteenth-century India.
